title: Limits of schemes along affine transition morphisms
statement: Let $I$ be a directed set and $(S_i,f_{ii'})$ an inverse system of schemes [def-pc-scheme] over $I$ whose transition morphisms $f_{ii'}:S_i\to S_{i'}$ ($i\ge i'$) are affine [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Then the limit $S=\varprojlim_iS_i$ exists in the category of schemes; each projection $f_i:S\to S_i$ is affine; and for every $0\in I$ and every open subscheme $U_0\subseteq S_0$, $f_0^{-1}(U_0)=\varprojlim_{i\ge0}f_{i0}^{-1}(U_0)$ in the category of schemes (with the restricted projections), the transition morphisms $f_{i0}^{-1}(U_0)\to f_{i'0}^{-1}(U_0)$ being affine. If all $S_i$ are affine, $S=\operatorname{Spec}(\varinjlim_i\Gamma(S_i,\mathcal O_{S_i}))$ (Limits, Lemma 01YW).

source.place: Lemma Tag 01YX (lemma-directed-inverse-system-has-limit, line 58) with Lemma Tag 01YW (lemma-directed-inverse-system-affine-schemes-has-limit, line 42)

proof.text: *Step 1 (reduction to $I_{\ge0}$).* If $I=\emptyset$ the limit is the terminal scheme $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ and the other clauses are void; so let $I\neq\emptyset$ (Stacks: a directed set is nonempty) and choose $0\in I$. The subset $I_{\ge0}$ is directed, and every $i\in I$ has some $j\in I_{\ge0}$ with $j\ge i$ ($I$ directed). View the system as a functor $D$ from the cofiltered category $\mathcal I$ ($\operatorname{Hom}(i,i')=\{*\}$ iff $i\ge i'$) to schemes; a limit of $D$ in schemes is a colimit of $D^{\mathrm{op}}:\mathcal I^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Sch}^{\mathrm{op}}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-initial-full-subcategory](1) with $\mathcal C=\mathrm{Sch}^{\mathrm{op}}$ and the full subcategory $\mathcal J=I_{\ge0}$, the limit of $D$ exists as soon as the limit of the restricted system $(S_i)_{i\ge0}$ exists, and then it is the same scheme, the projection to $S_i$ for arbitrary $i$ being $f_{ji}\circ f_j$ for any $j\ge i,0$. So it suffices to construct $\varprojlim_{i\ge0}S_i$.

source.place: Limits, Lemma 01YX (lemma-directed-inverse-system-has-limit), proof, first sentences ('Choose an element 0 in I. Note that I is nonempty as the limit is directed.')

proof.text: *Step 2 (the algebras $\mathcal A_i$).* For $i\ge0$ the morphism $f_{i0}:S_i\to S_0$ is affine (a transition morphism; $f_{00}=\mathrm{id}$). By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec](1) $\mathcal A_i:=f_{i0,*}\mathcal O_{S_i}$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{S_0}$-algebra, and by its part (3) $S_i\cong\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_{S_0}(\mathcal A_i)$ over $S_0$. For $i\ge i'\ge0$ the transition morphism $f_{ii'}$ is a morphism over $S_0$ ($f_{i'0}\circ f_{ii'}=f_{i0}$), so the functor of part (3) gives an $\mathcal O_{S_0}$-algebra map $\varphi_{ii'}=f_{i'0,*}(f_{ii'}^\sharp):\mathcal A_{i'}\to\mathcal A_i$; functoriality and $f_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$, $f_{i'i''}\circ f_{ii'}=f_{ii''}$ make $(\mathcal A_i,\varphi_{ii'})_{i\ge0}$ a directed system of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{S_0}$-algebras.

source.place: Limits, Lemma 01YX (lemma-directed-inverse-system-has-limit), proof ('consider the quasi-coherent sheaf of O_{S_0}-algebras A_i = f_{i0,*}O_{S_i}. Recall that S_i = Spec_{S_0}(A_i), see Morphisms, Lemma 01S8')

proof.text: *Step 3 (the colimit algebra).* By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra-colimit] the colimit $\mathcal A=\varinjlim_{i\ge0}\mathcal A_i$, with coprojections $\iota_i:\mathcal A_i\to\mathcal A$, is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{S_0}$-algebra, and for every affine open $U_0\subseteq S_0$ the map $\varinjlim_i\mathcal A_i(U_0)\to\mathcal A(U_0)$ induced by the $\iota_{i,U_0}$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Limits, Lemma 01YX (lemma-directed-inverse-system-has-limit), proof ('Set A = colim A_i. This is a quasi-coherent sheaf of O_{S_0}-algebras, see Schemes, Section 26.24')

proof.text: *Step 4 (the scheme $S$ and its projections).* Put $S=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_{S_0}(\mathcal A)$ with the affine structure morphism $f_0:S\to S_0$ of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec](2). Under the anti-equivalence of its part (3) (and the identifications $S_i\cong\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_{S_0}(\mathcal A_i)$ of Step 2), the coprojections $\iota_i$ correspond to $S_0$-morphisms $f_i:S\to S_i$, $i\ge0$ (for $i=0$ this is $f_0$, as $\iota_0$ composed with $\mathcal O_{S_0}\to\mathcal A_0$ is the structure map). Since $\iota_i\circ\varphi_{ii'}=\iota_{i'}$, functoriality gives $f_{ii'}\circ f_i=f_{i'}$ for $i\ge i'\ge0$: $(S,(f_i)_{i\ge0})$ is a cone over $(S_i)_{i\ge0}$.

source.place: Limits, Lemma 01YX (lemma-directed-inverse-system-has-limit), proof ('Set S = Spec_{S_0}(A). By Morphisms, Lemma 01SA we get for i >= 0 morphisms f_i : S -> S_i compatible with the transition morphisms')

proof.text: *Step 5 (the limit over an affine open of $S_0$; Lemma 01YW).* Let $U_0\subseteq S_0$ be an affine open, $U_i=f_{i0}^{-1}(U_0)$ ($i\ge0$) and $U=f_0^{-1}(U_0)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec](2),(3) there are isomorphisms $U_i\cong\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal A_i(U_0)$ (note $\mathcal A_i(U_0)=\Gamma(U_i,\mathcal O_{S_i})$) and $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal A(U_0)$ under which the restricted transition morphisms $U_i\to U_{i'}$ are $\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi_{ii',U_0})$ and the restricted projections $U\to U_i$ are $\operatorname{Spec}(\iota_{i,U_0})$. By Step 3, $(\mathcal A(U_0),(\iota_{i,U_0}))$ is the colimit of the rings $\mathcal A_i(U_0)$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-colimit-limit] $(U,(f_i|_U)_{i\ge0})$ is a limit of the system $(U_i)_{i\ge0}$ in the category of schemes. Explicitly: for every scheme $V$ and morphisms $h_i:V\to U_i$ with $f_{ii'}\circ h_i=h_{i'}$ there is exactly one $h:V\to U$ with $f_i\circ h=h_i$ for all $i\ge0$.

source.place: Limits, Lemma 01YX (lemma-directed-inverse-system-has-limit), proof ('By Lemma 01YW above we see that for any affine open U_0 in S_0 the inverse image U = f_0^{-1}(U_0) is the limit of the system of opens U_i = f_{i0}^{-1}(U_0), i >= 0 in the category of schemes'); Limits, Lemma 01YW (line 42)

proof.text: *Step 6 (uniqueness, locally).* Let $W$ be a scheme and $h,h':W\to S$ morphisms with $f_i\circ h=f_i\circ h'$ for all $i\ge0$. Then $h=h'$. Indeed, let $w\in W$ and choose an affine open $U_0\subseteq S_0$ containing $f_0(h(w))=f_0(h'(w))$; put $U=f_0^{-1}(U_0)$ and $W_w=h^{-1}(U)=(f_0\circ h)^{-1}(U_0)=(f_0\circ h')^{-1}(U_0)=h'^{-1}(U)$, an open neighbourhood of $w$. The restrictions $h|_{W_w},h'|_{W_w}:W_w\to U$ have the same composites $f_i\circ h|_{W_w}=f_i\circ h'|_{W_w}:W_w\to U_i$, so they are equal by the uniqueness in Step 5. The $W_w$ cover $W$, hence $h=h'$ by the uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing].

source.place: Limits, Lemma 01YX (lemma-directed-inverse-system-has-limit), proof (the 'uniqueness property' invoked for the glueing, written out)

proof.text: *Step 7 ($S$ is the limit).* Let $T$ be a scheme and $g_i:T\to S_i$ ($i\ge0$) morphisms with $f_{ii'}\circ g_i=g_{i'}$. For $t\in T$ choose an affine open $U_0\subseteq S_0$ containing $g_0(t)$ and an affine open $V\ni t$ of $T$ with $V\subseteq g_0^{-1}(U_0)$ (the affine opens of a scheme form a basis of its topology [def-pc-scheme]: every point has an affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}R$, whose principal opens $D(r)\cong\operatorname{Spec}R_r$ form a basis). For $i\ge0$, $f_{i0}(g_i(V))=g_0(V)\subseteq U_0$, so $g_i|_V$ factors through $U_i=f_{i0}^{-1}(U_0)$, compatibly in $i$; by Step 5 there is a unique $g_V:V\to U=f_0^{-1}(U_0)\subseteq S$ with $f_i\circ g_V=g_i|_V$ for all $i\ge0$. These $V$ cover $T$. For two of them, $g_V|_{V\cap V'}$ and $g_{V'}|_{V\cap V'}$ have the same composites $g_i|_{V\cap V'}$ with every $f_i$, so they agree by Step 6. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] the $g_V$ glue to $g:T\to S$ with $g|_V=g_V$; then $(f_i\circ g)|_V=g_i|_V$ for every $V$ of the cover, so $f_i\circ g=g_i$ (uniqueness clause of the same lemma). If $g':T\to S$ also satisfies $f_i\circ g'=g_i$ for all $i\ge0$, then $g'=g$ by Step 6. Hence $(S,(f_i)_{i\ge0})$ is a limit of $(S_i)_{i\ge0}$ in the category of schemes, and by Step 1 $S=\varprojlim_{i\in I}S_i$.

source.place: Limits, Lemma 01YX (lemma-directed-inverse-system-has-limit), proof, second paragraph ('Let T be a scheme. Let g_i : T -> S_i be a compatible system of morphisms ... The morphisms g_V glue to a morphism g : T -> S because of the uniqueness property')

proof.text: *Step 8 (the projections are affine; the limit commutes with opens of a stage).* Now that the limit $(S,(f_i)_{i\in I})$ exists, [lem-weil-pbc-limit-cone-affine-projections-opens](1) shows that every $f_i:S\to S_i$, $i\in I$, is affine, and its part (2) shows, for every $0\in I$ and every open $U_0\subseteq S_0$, that the restricted transition morphisms $f_{i0}^{-1}(U_0)\to f_{i'0}^{-1}(U_0)$ are affine and that $f_0^{-1}(U_0)$ with the restricted projections is $\varprojlim_{i\ge0}f_{i0}^{-1}(U_0)$ in the category of schemes. (Stacks obtains (1) from Morphisms, Lemma 01SG (affine permanence) and (2) 'from the construction'; the cited node gives both for any limit cone, which is what the users of this lemma apply.)

source.place: Limits, Lemma 01YX (lemma-directed-inverse-system-has-limit), proof ('Note that the morphisms f_i are affine by Morphisms, Lemma 01SG' and 'The final statement is clear from the construction of the limit above')

proof.text: *Step 9 (the affine case, Lemma 01YW).* If all $S_i$ are affine, write $R_i=\Gamma(S_i,\mathcal O_{S_i})$; the transition morphisms give ring maps $R_{i'}\to R_i$ ($i\ge i'$), a directed system with colimit $R=\varinjlim_iR_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-colimit-limit], $\operatorname{Spec}R$ with the morphisms induced by the coprojections is a limit of the system $(\operatorname{Spec}R_i)\cong(S_i)$ (each $S_i\cong\operatorname{Spec}R_i$ canonically, $S_i$ being affine). Two limits of the same system are isomorphic by a unique isomorphism compatible with the projections, so $S\cong\operatorname{Spec}(\varinjlim_i\Gamma(S_i,\mathcal O_{S_i}))$; in particular $S$ is affine.

source.place: Limits, Lemma 01YW (lemma-directed-inverse-system-affine-schemes-has-limit, line 42), proof ('Just define S = Spec(colim R_i)')

lean.statement: theorem exists_limit_affine_transition {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] [Nonempty I] (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ Scheme.{u}) [∀ {i j : Iᵒᵖ} (f : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map f)] : ∃ c : Cone D, Nonempty (IsLimit c) ∧ (∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, IsAffineHom (c.π.app i)) ∧ (∀ (i : Iᵒᵖ) (U : (D.obj i).Opens), Nonempty (IsLimit (opensCone D c i U)) ∧ ∀ {j k : Over i} (f : j ⟶ k), IsAffineHom ((opensDiagram D i U).map f)) ∧ ((∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, IsAffine (D.obj i)) → ∃ e : c.pt ≅ Spec (colimit (D.op ⋙ Scheme.Γ)), ∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, e.hom ≫ Spec.map (colimit.ι (D.op ⋙ Scheme.Γ) (op i)) = c.π.app i ≫ (ΓSpec.adjunction.unit.app (D.obj i)))

reviewed_lean.note: directed set = Preorder+IsDirected+Nonempty (Stacks nonempty, no stage fixed); D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ Scheme.{u}; affine transitions = instance IsAffineHom (D.map f); limit exists = ∃ c, Nonempty (IsLimit c); projections IsAffineHom; per stage i and arbitrary open U: Mathlib opensCone is limit (Over i = upper tail of I), restricted transitions IsAffineHom; affine case iso c.pt ≅ Spec(colimit Γ) compatible via Spec.map colimit.ι and ΓSpec unit; #check opensCone/opensDiagram are Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry, types of unit and Spec.map checked; I : Type u tied to Scheme.{u} as Mathlib/NoetherianApproximation
